title: The Risk Practice in Context

header.html: Apply the risk practice: risk management approach, risk register; areas of focus of key roles; threats and opportunities, risk appetite and tolerance, the five risk steps, owners and responses; analyze whether a risk approach is effective and fit for purpose considering the principles, the techniques and tailoring
the official PRINCE2 7 Practitioner syllabus (PeopleCert, version 7.2)

toc.title: Areas of focus of the key roles

html:
1Purpose, objectives and principles

The risk practice gives the project a structured way to deal with uncertainty. A risk is something that might happen and would affect an objective. It can be a threat or an opportunity. A risk is described by its cause, the event and the effect. If it has already happened, it is an issue, not a risk.

It serves continued business justification (risks affect the case), manage by exception (risk tolerance triggers escalation), define roles (every risk has an owner), learn from experience (past risks guide identification) and manage by stages (risks are reviewed at each boundary).

Exam tip

. Might happen is a risk; has happened is an issue. If a scenario says the supplier is already late, do not treat it as a risk.

2The key management products

Product What it is for
Risk management approach How risk is managed on this project: roles, scales for probability and impact, risk appetite and tolerance, response types, reporting. Part of the initiation documentation
Risk register A record of each risk: description, owner, assessment, responses, status. Part of the project log and updated all the time

Risk appetite is how much risk the organization is willing to take to reach its objectives. Risk tolerance is the limit of exposure that is acceptable at a level; beyond it, the risk is escalated.

Exam tip

. Approach says how; register says what. The scales and tolerances are agreed once in the approach; the individual risks live in the register.

3Areas of focus of the key roles

Role Focus in the risk practice
Executive Accountable that risk is managed and the approach suits the business case
Senior user Risks to user needs and benefits
Senior supplier Risks in the supplier's work and resources
Project manager Creates the approach and register; makes sure risks are identified, assessed and controlled
Team manager Raises risks from the work; manages those assigned
Project assurance Checks risk procedures are followed
Project support Keeps the register and analysis up to date

A risk owner is accountable for managing one risk and needs the authority to do it. A risk action owner carries out a response action for the owner. The owner is often not the person who does the work. Check the book's table for exact responsibilities.

4Effective management and techniques

Step What happens
Identify Find risks and write them as cause, event and effect, using lessons and the people involved
Assess Rate probability, impact and proximity (when); compare exposure with the tolerance
Plan Choose a response; name the owner and action owners
Implement Carry out the response and monitor its effect
Communicate Share risk information with stakeholders; escalate what exceeds the tolerance

Responses to threats include avoid, reduce, fallback, transfer, accept and share. Responses to opportunities include exploit, enhance, share and reject. Reduce makes a threat less likely or smaller; transfer moves the financial impact to another party; exploit makes an opportunity more certain.

After a response, some residual risk remains, and a response can create a secondary risk. Both are assessed and recorded. Risks are reviewed regularly: at each stage boundary and in routine progress reporting.

Exam tip

. Escalate when the exposure goes beyond the tolerance of your level. The project manager keeps risks that fit the stage tolerance and sends the rest to the board.

5Judging a scenario

An effective approach Red flags (not fit for purpose)
Each risk has an owner with authority (define roles) Risks with no owner, or the whole list owned by one person
Assessed for probability, impact and proximity Only a vague "high or low", no timing
Opportunities recorded and managed with threats Only threats are recorded
Reviewed regularly and at every stage boundary Register written at initiation and never reopened
Escalated to the right level when tolerance is exceeded (manage by exception) Project manager sits on a risk beyond the tolerance, or sends every risk to the board
Residual and secondary risks recorded Risk closed as soon as a response is chosen
Appetite and tolerance agreed in the approach Each person uses their own scales

Tailoring.

Context How risk management changes
Small internal project A one-page approach and short register reviewed at each checkpoint
Agile or hybrid delivery Risks reviewed at each sprint review; the backlog carries risk-driven items
Large or multi-party project Shared risks across suppliers, with owners named in each organization and escalation paths in the contract
Sustainability or data concerns Sustainability, data and security risks are assessed like any other
Exam tip

. A risk without an owner is not managed. The first check on any risk scenario is who owns it, then whether it was assessed, then whether it is at the right level.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1On a small internal project to update berth signs, Sam Okafor keeps a one-page risk management approach and a short risk register with named owners, reviewed at each checkpoint. Was this appropriate?

  • AYes, because the approach is scaled to the project while risks keep owners and review
  • BYes, because a small project does not need to manage its risks in any formal way
  • CNo, because every project must use the full risk management approach in the same detail
  • DNo, because risks on a small project should be left to the project board to manage
Show the answer

Answer: A. Tailoring scales the approach, and the register keeps owners, assessment and review, which preserves the intent of the practice.

S2Marta Quinn agrees that Sam Okafor owns the risk of a late test environment. Wei Chen's team will order the extra environment as the agreed response. Which statement describes Wei Chen's role in relation to the risk?

  • AHe is the risk owner, accountable for managing the risk as a whole
  • BHe is a risk action owner, carrying out the response for the owner
  • CHe is the change authority, deciding whether the response goes ahead
  • DHe is project assurance, checking the response independently of the team
Show the answer

Answer: B. Wei carries out a response action for the owner, who stays accountable for managing the risk.

S3A supplier risk on Project Harbor now has an exposure beyond the project's risk tolerance, and Sam Okafor cannot respond within his authority. What should he do?

  • AAccept the risk and note the decision in the daily log for the next review
  • BWait for the next highlight report and mention the risk to the board then
  • CEscalate it to the project board with the assessment and the options
  • DAsk Wei Chen to take ownership of the risk and deal with it in the team
Show the answer

Answer: C. Risk that exceeds the tolerance of the project manager's level must be escalated, as manage by exception requires.

S4Sam Okafor wants the agreed scales for probability and impact, and the risk appetite and tolerance, written once so everyone assesses risks the same way. Which management product holds them?

  • AIssue management approach
  • BQuality management approach
  • CChange management approach
  • DRisk management approach
Show the answer

Answer: D. The risk management approach sets scales, appetite and tolerance, while the other approaches cover issues, quality and change; the register holds the individual risks.

S5Tomas Reyes suggests reusing a payment module from another port, which could cut build cost. Sam Okafor records it in the risk register as an opportunity, names an owner and asks the team to assess a response. Was this appropriate?

  • AYes, because opportunities are uncertain events handled with the same steps as threats
  • BYes, because opportunities should be managed through change control and not as risks
  • CNo, because the risk register holds threats only, and opportunities go in the business case
  • DNo, because the idea should be ignored until it has actually happened to the project
Show the answer

Answer: A. The practice covers threats and opportunities, and both are identified, assessed, planned and tracked in the register.

S6To reduce the risk of a late build, Sam Okafor adds a second supplier team, then marks the risk closed. The extra team might cause integration problems. What should he have done?

  • AClose the risk and ignore the new concern until it has actually happened
  • BRecord the residual and secondary risks with owners, and keep reviewing them
  • CAsk the board to request an exception plan without assessing the new concern
  • DPass the risk to Marta Quinn at once without any assessment of the extra team
Show the answer

Answer: B. A response can leave a residual risk and create a secondary risk, and both must be assessed, owned and reviewed.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Name the five risk steps.

Show the answer

Identify, assess, plan, implement and communicate.

R2What is the difference between risk appetite and risk tolerance?

Show the answer

Appetite is how much risk the organization is willing to take; tolerance is the limit of acceptable exposure at a level.

R3Who is accountable for managing a risk?

Show the answer

The risk owner.

R4What is a secondary risk?

Show the answer

A new risk created by a response to another risk.

R5What three aspects are assessed for each risk?

Show the answer

Probability, impact and proximity.

R6Which risk is a risk and not an issue?

Show the answer

One that might happen; if it has already happened, it is an issue.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Risk threat or opportunity from uncertainty: cause, event, effect
Five steps identify, assess, plan, implement, communicate
Assessment probability, impact and proximity against the tolerance
Appetite and tolerance willingness to take risk; limit that triggers escalation
Owner and action owner owner is accountable; action owner does the action
Risk management approach scales, roles, appetite, tolerance
Risk register each risk, owner, responses, status
Residual and secondary assessed and recorded after every response
